title: Statewide health-record model predicts one-year coronary heart disease risk
summary: An XGBoost pipeline with feature selection and isotonic calibration was trained on a retrospective Maine Health Information Exchange cohort (N = 1,042,124) and validated on a later prospective cohort (N = 1,040,158). The AUC was 0.952 (95% CI 0.950-0.954) in the retrospective cohort and 0.888 (0.885-0.890) in the later cohort. Of 19 people in the very-high-risk group, 11 (57.89%) developed CHD within one year. Data come from one state and are from health records.
ai_technology: XGBoost feature selection and risk prediction with isotonic calibration on electronic health records
organization: Guangdong Polytechnic Normal University; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Temporal validation in a 2016-2018 cohort after training on 2015-2017 data.
evidence.unknown: Performance in other states and effect on prevention outcomes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts one-year CHD risk and stratifies a population into five risk categories.
